name: Shri Sant Balbir Singh
education: Pre-University Educated at Govt. School Nihaluwal, Distt. Jalandhar, Punjab
profession: Social Reformer, Environmentalist and Spiritual Leader
present_address: Flat No. 102, Brahmaputra Complex, Dr. B.D. Marg, New Delhi - 110001
permanent_address: House No.159, Village – Sichewal Tehsil – Shankot, District Jalandhar, Punjab
social_activities: President, Ek Onkar Charitable Trust, Seechewal; the social reformer (known as ‘welfare Baba’); environmentalist; cleaned the 165 Km long rivulet, The Holy Kali Bein; established Seechewal Model, a simple, easy and economical method to treat and reuse wastewater for agricultural purposes; established Nawan Nanakan Charitable School at Sultanpur Lodhi, where free education is provided to the children of poor migrant labourers from Bihar and other States; engaged in relief work by providing food and other essentials to the victims of floods and other natural calamities; associated with conservation of natural water resources including rivers, drains, wetlands, etc.; undertook construction/renovation of roads in remote and backward areas; involved in tree plantations and more than 5 lakh saplings have been grown in the nursery located at Nirmal Kuteya, Seechewal and distributed free of cost; contributed immensely towards eradication of social injustice, poverty and such other issues; worked for the promotion of communal harmony; started 'Avtar Community Radio 90.4' which is being run to spread environmental and social awareness
hobbies: Organises annual sports tournaments of wrestling, boxing, hockey, kabaddi, volleyball, tug of war, gatka, athletics, water sports, at Seechewal and Sultanpur Lodhi; organises training programmes in hockey, boxing, gatka, wrestling, kabaddi, water sports, etc.
countries_visited: England to attend International Conference of World Religious Leaders on Climate Change which is organised by ECO Sikh organization in collaboration with UNESCO, 2009; Denmark to attend International Conference of Religious Saints on Climate Change organized by UNO, 2009; U.S.A., Canada, Pakistan, France, Italy and U.K.
other_information: Head, Nirmal Kuteya Seechewal; Patron, Nirmal Noor, an environmental tri-lingual magazine; unanimously elected as Sarpanch of Seechewal consecutively for two terms; acclaimed by Time Magazine as ‘The Hero of Environment’; praised as the preacher of ‘A Noble Mission’ by former President of India, Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam and hailed his work as a major technological achievement of India besides mentioning about his contributions in national and international speeches; recipient of several awards including, (i) Padma Shri, 2017, (ii) Nirmal Gram Puraskar, 2008 by the then Hon’ble President of India, (iii) Panj Pani Award, 2006, by Doordarshan, Jalandhar on World Environment Day, (iv) Living Legend Award, 2007, by People’s Forum, Kot Kapura, (v) Punjab Rattan Award, 2007, 2009 by Dainik Bhaskar newspaper, (vi) ‘Excellence Among Sikhs’, 2008 by US based social organization SCORE, (vii) Madhu Bhasin Award, 2009 by Guru Jambheshwara University of Science and Technology, Hisar, (viii) Nirmal Gram Puraskar, 2009 by Punjab Government, (ix) State Award on Independence Day, 2009, by the Chief Minister of Punjab, and (x) SAARC Environment Award, 2010; awarded (i) D.Litt honoris causa by Punjabi University, Patiala and (ii) Fellowship by Punjab Academy of Sciences, Patiala, Punjab; honoured/felicitated by many Institutes/NGOs / Govt. Authorities/ Colleges/ Universities, and others for his selfless public welfare services to humanity/education/ environment which include, (i) All India Pingalwara Charitable Trust, Amritsar, 2004, (ii) Punjab Pollution Control Board on World Environment Day, 2005, (iii) Punjab and Haryana High Court Bar Council, Chandigarh, 2008, (iv) Punjabi University, Patiala, 2009, (vii) Dalai Lama, Dharamshala, 2010, (v) Parliament of Canada, 2010, (vi) District Administration, Kapurthala, 2010 and (vii) DAV College, Amritsar, 2011
